newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up in spot, forward markets on supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up in spot, forward markets on supply.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended a day of range-bound trade at 35.7575/7625 per dollar, up from opening quotes of 35.765/775 on good supply of the US currency and poor demand, dealers said on Monday.
They said the State Bank of India (SBI) bought dollars but the rupee moved up as supply exceeded demand.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, did not buy dollars on Monday in either the spot or forward markets.
Dealers said the rupee traded at an intraday high of 35.7550 and a low of 35.7725 per dollar.

"Good dollar supplies pushed the rupee down to 35.7575, with stray deals at 35.7550," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Then the SBI bought dollars and the rupee dropped to 35.765 before moving up again of fresh dollar sales."
Dealers said the rupee ended up against the forward dollar also on exporter sales.
"There was little action, it was a very dull day," said a dealer. "There was some dollar sales by exporters and premia dropped."
Dealers said the annualised premia for six-month dollars ended Monday at 4.42 percent against the weekend close of 4.47.
